title: How to Compare Commercial Lease Proposals
excerpt: Compare lease proposals on total cost, risk, suitability and flexibility rather than advertised rent alone.
author: Joe Kelley
metaTitle: How to Compare Commercial Leases | Your Office Space
metaDescription: A practical framework for comparing commercial lease proposals on cost, suitability, risk and flexibility.
body:
Two lease proposals can show similar rent and create very different business outcomes. A useful comparison puts every option on the same basis.

## Build one assumptions sheet

Use the same lease start date, term, area basis and forecast period. Record what is included, excluded or still unverified.

## Compare the full occupancy cost

Include base rent, outgoings, parking, utilities, fitout contribution, rent-free periods, relocation costs, review mechanisms and likely make-good exposure. Keep estimates clearly labelled and update them when evidence arrives.

## Test operational suitability

Cost is only one part of the decision. Score location, team access, customer access, layout efficiency, building services, accessibility, signage, parking and growth capacity against the written brief.

## Compare legal and commercial risk

Ask a commercial property lawyer to review the documents. Pay particular attention to security, guarantees, repair obligations, permitted use, relocation, redevelopment, assignment, subletting, options and default provisions.

## Show uncertainty rather than hiding it

If a figure or condition is unknown, flag it. A transparent comparison is more useful than a precise-looking model built on assumptions.

## Decide with a record

Keep the shortlist, assumptions, adviser input and reasons for the final decision. This gives stakeholders a clear approval trail.

Your Office Space can coordinate the brief, property search and commercial comparison while your legal and financial advisers cover their specialist areas.
